evidence: lib/state/anki.js:106-108 runs `const napped = await disableAppNap(...)` then `const wasRunning = await isRunning('Anki')` then `const launched = wasRunning ? false : await launchHeadless('Anki')`: only `launched` depends on `wasRunning`, so the independent `disableAppNap` call needlessly gates the isRunning->launch chain. This is the partial-dependency waterfall the rule names; no `better-all` and no promise-first pattern is used anywhere in the repo.
fix: Use the rule's dependency-based form in lib/state/anki.js:106: `const nappedP = disableAppNap(ANKI_BUNDLE_IDS); const runP = isRunning('Anki'); const launchedP = runP.then(r => (r ? false : launchHeadless('Anki'))); const [napped, wasRunning, launched] = await Promise.all([nappedP, runP, launchedP]);` so App Nap disabling overlaps the running-check and the launch.

lib/server.js:563-567 `serveFile` does `fs.existsSync(file)` then `fs.readFileSync(file)` on every request, and it is the handler for the three shipped static pages: web/dashboard.html (lib/server.js:546), web/panel.html (lib/server.js:552) and web/debug.html (lib/server.js:555). Nothing caches the bytes, so each page load re-reads the file from disk inside a long-lived daemon process. This is the rule's Incorrect 'reads the file on every request' shape.
fix: Add an mtime-gated module-level cache rather than a plain module-level read, because lib/server.js:51-66 `assetStamp()` and the panel's self-reload depend on an edit to web/panel.html reaching the open window. For example: `const assetCache = new Map(); function serveFile(res, file, type) { let st; try { st = fs.statSync(file); } catch { return json(res, 404, {...}); } const hit = assetCache.get(file); const body = hit && hit.mtimeMs === st.mtimeMs ? hit.body : fs.readFileSync(file); assetCache.set(file, { mtimeMs: st.mtimeMs, body }); ... }` which pays one stat instead of a full read when the file has not changed and preserves the live-reload contract.

evidence: The five Playwright UI specs have no explicit timeout and no CI branch anywhere: `grep -rn 'process.env' test/` returns nothing, and no spec calls `page.setDefaultTimeout`/`setDefaultNavigationTimeout` or passes a `timeout` to `chromium.launch` or `page.goto` (test/immersive-layout.pw.mjs:11,15; test/forfeit-legible.pw.mjs:7,12; test/immersive-menu.pw.mjs:12,17; test/latency-indicator.pw.mjs:10,15; test/star-calendar.pw.mjs:9,14). test/immersive-layout.pw.mjs:21 uses a fixed `await page.waitForTimeout(150)` with no CI multiplier, and the node suite has the same fixed sleeps with no CI branch (test/watcher.test.js:69,88,111,129,160 at 120/250/150/100/200ms, test/system.test.js:25 at 600ms, test/panel.test.js:71 at 30ms). node --test's per-test timeout defaults to Infinity, so a spec that stalls hangs the run rather than failing it.

evidence: Nothing asserts an executed test count, and the failure mode is live right now. .github/workflows/ci.yml:22 runs `test ! -f package-lock.json && echo "zero-dependency by design"`, but package-lock.json has been tracked since commit f8c8dfd; running that line locally exits 1, and `gh run view 32265359047 --log-failed` shows `##[error]Process completed with exit code 1` on that step, so the `node --test` step at .github/workflows/ci.yml:24 never executes and CI has run ZERO tests on every push since. Separately, the runner itself cannot report a zero-selection as a failure: `node --test 'test/nosuch*.test.js'` prints `tests 0 / pass 0 / fail 0` and exits 0, and `node --test test/definitely-missing.test.js` prints `Could not find` and also exits 0 (verified on node v23.11.0).
fix: Fix the gate and then assert the count. Replace .github/workflows/ci.yml:21-22 with a check that matches the repo's actual state (the lockfile is intended now, so drop the step or assert `test -f package-lock.json`), and make the test step assert a floor, e.g. `node --test --test-reporter=tap test/*.test.js | tee /tmp/tap.txt; n=$(grep -c '^ok ' /tmp/tap.txt); echo "executed $n"; test "$n" -ge 275` so a glob or discovery change that selects nothing turns the build red instead of green.

evidence: No literal-detector ships at all: `.git/hooks` contains only the stock `.sample` files, there is no husky/lint-staged/pre-commit config in the repo, and .github/workflows/ci.yml has no such step (the hooks/ directory holds Interstice's own on-submit.sh/on-stop.sh Claude Code hooks, unrelated to commits). The literals it is meant to block are present: 21 assertions compare against a bare integer count (test/focus-blocks.test.js:20,31,41,61,71; test/engine.test.js:117,128,132,138; test/ocr.test.js:33,39,87,100,123,137; test/video-probe.test.js:35; test/focus-store.test.js:21,62; test/watcher.test.js:89,94,112,117), and hardcoded dates appear on the assertion side rather than being derived from the fixture, for example test/focus-blocks.test.js:83 `assert.equal(out[0].day, '2026-08-20', ...)` and test/stars-routes.test.js:37-39 asserting `'2026-08-19'` and `'2026-08-19T09:00:00-07:00'` that are re-typed from the stub literals at test/stars-routes.test.js:9-10.
fix: Add a pre-commit gate (a `.githooks/pre-commit` wired with `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`, plus the same command as a CI step) that greps staged files under test/ for `assert\.(equal|strictEqual|deepEqual)\([^,]+,\s*([0-9]+|'\d{4}-\d{2}(-\d{2})?)` and exits non-zero, with an explicit allowlist comment marker for the cases that are genuinely about the literal. Then derive the flagged values from the fixture, e.g. name the stub's date once in test/stars-routes.test.js (`const DAY = '2026-08-19'`) and assert against `DAY`, and assert `out.length === fixture.length` style relations instead of bare 1s where the count follows from the fixture.

evidence: The construct does not exist here: Interstice has no 'find a solution' or 'find a valid X' surface. The nearest thing, lib/router.js:67-71 `nextAvailableFrom`, walks a fixed four-item ladder (`config.ladder`, constrained to the `KNOWN_RUNGS` set at lib/config.js:4) in order and returns `null` when nothing qualifies, so it never claims a solution exists without producing it; web/panel.html and web/dashboard.html render deliveries and statistics rather than searching a solution space. There is no combinatorial claim in the product for an enumerator to prove.

Two gates guarding this batch's locality cannot do both jobs. .github/workflows/ci.yml:22 `test ! -f package-lock.json && echo "zero-dependency by design"` can never pass now that package-lock.json is tracked (commit f8c8dfd added @playwright/test): it exits 1 locally, and `gh run view 32265359047 --log-failed` confirms `##[error]Process completed with exit code 1` on that step, which also aborts the job before the `node --test` step at .github/workflows/ci.yml:24. Conversely the test gate cannot fail when it is broken: `node --test 'test/nosuch*.test.js'` prints `tests 0 / pass 0 / fail 0` and exits 0, and `node --test test/definitely-missing.test.js` prints `Could not find` and still exits 0 (node v23.11.0), so an empty selection reads as green evidence.
fix: Rewrite .github/workflows/ci.yml:21-22 so it asserts the invariant the repo actually holds (either `node -e "const p=require('./package.json'); if (Object.keys(p.dependencies||{}).length) process.exit(1)"` for 'no runtime dependencies', or delete the step), and give the test step a failing-mode: capture TAP output and assert `ok` count >= the known floor as in TC-007, so zero-selected tests fail the build. Then verify each gate twice, once against a known-good tree and once against a deliberately broken one, before trusting it.
